name: PageErrorBoundary

props.description: What replaces the page that threw. Default: <ErrorSurface mode="application" status={500} titleLevel={1}> with the kit's localized title/description and ONE 'Reload page' action. The function form gets the error and a `reset()` that draws the page again without a reload.
props.name: fallback

props.description: Draw the page again when this value changes (Object.is). The boundary ALREADY resets when the URL changes — it records the URL it failed on and resets on the next render under a different one, so it needs no router integration; pass a key only for a change the URL does not show.
props.name: resetKey

props.description: Report the error (an error tracker). Replaces the development-time console.error.
props.name: onError

related: AppShell — wraps its children in a PageErrorBoundary by default (`errorBoundary`).
ErrorSurface — the default fallback; use it directly for an HTTP 400/403/404/500/503 page the server reports.
tagline: Page-level React error boundary (gh#1494): a page that throws while rendering is replaced by an application ErrorSurface and the shell around it stays. AppShell wraps its children in one by default; use this directly only around a page outside AppShell.
usage: DO rely on AppShell's built-in boundary: every page inside AppShell is already covered. Configure it with AppShell `errorBoundary={{ onError: report }}`.
DO wrap a page that renders OUTSIDE AppShell (a CenteredShell page, an embedded view) in <PageErrorBoundary> yourself.
DO NOT wrap every Card in a boundary: it is PAGE-level. An in-page query failure is DataState / Alert.QueryError, not a render error.
DO NOT key the boundary on the URL yourself to make it reset — it already resets on navigation.
useCases: A list page whose row renderer hits an unexpected null: the page area shows the ErrorSurface, the sidebar still works, and navigating to another page draws that page normally.
